title: Javascript Expressions in JSX & ES6 Template Literals
summary: Shows how to embed JavaScript inside JSX with curly braces, why only expressions (not statements) are allowed, and several ways to build a full name including ES6 template literals.

concepts.heading: Curly braces inject JavaScript into JSX
points: Text placed inside a JSX element is treated as a literal string. Writing Hello name prints the word name, not the variable.

Wrapping something in {} switches back to JavaScript:

Hello {name}

outputs the value stored in the const name.
JSX therefore works in both directions: HTML inside a JS file, and JS inside that HTML.

concepts.heading: Any expression works
points: Inside the braces you can put any JavaScript expression: a variable, maths such as {3 + 9}, or a function call like {Math.floor(Math.random() * 10)}, which yields a random whole number from 0 to 9 and changes on each page refresh.
Math.random() gives a decimal in [0,1); multiply by 10 to scale it, and Math.floor rounds down.

concepts.heading: Expressions vs statements
points: An expression evaluates to a value. A statement (if/else, loops) performs work and does not produce a value, so it is not allowed in the braces; an if (name === ...) block there is a syntax error.
(Extra) For conditional output inside JSX use the ternary operator or && instead; these are covered in a later lesson.

concepts.heading: Building a full name: three approaches
points: Concatenation inside one pair of braces: {fName + " " + lName}.
Two separate brace pairs with a literal space between them: {fName} {lName}. Multiple brace pairs in one element are fine.

ES6 template literal: backticks with ${} placeholders, for example `${fName} ${lName}`. Wrapped in JSX braces this nests three levels (string inside template inside JSX inside JS), so the simpler options are generally clearer.
Any approach that gives the right output is acceptable.

concepts.heading: Rules of thumb
points: Multiple top-level elements still need a single wrapper such as a div.
The completed sandbox is in the resources to experiment with.

task.name: Lucky number and full name
task.starting_point: Starter sandbox rendering one h1 from a name const
task.goal: Display values from JavaScript variables and expressions inside JSX
steps: Replace the hard-coded text with {name} to render a const.
Create a const num set to your lucky number and add a paragraph with the text Your lucky number is plus {num}.
Wrap the h1 and p in a div so render receives one element.
Experiment with expressions such as {3 + 9} and a random number using Math.random and Math.floor.
Create fName and lName consts and show the full name in an h1 in at least two different ways.
task.expected_result: Heading showing the full name, paragraph showing the lucky number (or a random/calculated value).
task.reference_repo_path: Section 36 - React.js/36.07 Javascript Expressions in JSX & ES6 Template Literals

pitfalls: Forgetting braces prints the variable name as plain text.
Statements such as if/else inside braces cause syntax errors; only expressions are allowed.
Sibling elements without a parent wrapper break render.
